skill.name: sparc-methodology
skill.description: Guide structured software delivery with SPARC phases, TDD practices, and Claude Flow multi-agent coordination examples.
skill.summary: Plan, implement, test, review, and document software with the SPARC methodology.
skill.author: Claude Flow

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks and fenced Claude Flow MCP examples. Several bash examples are confirmed medium-risk external command guidance because they ask users to run npx or local claude-flow commands. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or malicious workflow logic was found in the reviewed skill content.

remediation.suggestion: Pin claude-flow package versions in every npx example and instruct users to review the package source before execution.
Add a clear warning that CLI commands require explicit user approval and should run only in trusted project directories.
Avoid claude-flow@alpha examples in default workflows, or explain the stability and trust tradeoffs before use.

content.value_statement: Complex software work can lose structure across planning, coding, testing, and review. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a SPARC workflow for phased delivery and multi-agent coordination.
actual_capabilities: Explains the SPARC phases from specification through completion.
Documents specialized modes for coding, architecture, testing, review, research, and documentation.
Shows Claude Flow MCP examples for swarm setup, agent spawning, memory, and monitoring.
Provides CLI workflows for feature development, bug investigation, performance work, and full pipelines.
Defines TDD, review, memory, hook, documentation, and file organization practices.
limitations: Requires Claude Flow MCP tools or CLI access for examples to run as written.
Acts as workflow guidance and does not implement project code by itself.
Includes external command examples that users should review before running.
Performance claims are presented by the skill and are not independently validated here.

use_cases.title: Plan a Feature Delivery Flow
use_cases.description: Break a feature into specification, architecture, TDD implementation, review, and documentation steps.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Multi-Agent Engineering Work
use_cases.description: Assign research, coding, testing, review, and documentation responsibilities across specialized agents.

use_cases.title: Standardize Quality Practices
use_cases.description: Apply consistent TDD, review, memory, and documentation practices across repeatable software workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a SPARC Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the SPARC methodology to plan this feature: [feature]. Include requirements, architecture questions, test ideas, review checks, and completion criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Create a TDD Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a SPARC TDD workflow for [feature]. Define the red, green, and refactor steps, the test coverage target, and the review checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Specialist Agents
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-agent SPARC plan for [project]. Assign roles for research, architecture, coding, testing, review, optimization, and documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Full Delivery Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this software delivery workflow with SPARC: [workflow]. Identify missing phases, weak quality gates, coordination risks, and concrete improvements.

output_examples.input: Plan a user authentication feature with SPARC.
output: Specification: define login, logout, password reset, session rules, and security constraints.
Architecture: choose token handling, storage boundaries, API contracts, and error handling paths.
Refinement: write failing authentication tests, implement minimal behavior, then refactor.
Completion: run review checks, update API documentation, and capture decisions in memory.

output_examples.input: Coordinate a legacy refactor with specialist agents.
output: Analyzer reviews dependencies, risky modules, and change impact.
Tester builds a regression safety net before refactoring begins.
Coder performs incremental changes while reviewer checks maintainability and behavior.
Documenter records migration steps and remaining technical debt.

output_examples.input: Improve a slow API using the SPARC workflow.
output_examples.output: The workflow starts with performance profiling, then designs a caching or query strategy, implements changes under tests, benchmarks results, and documents operational limits.

best_practices: Start with clear requirements, constraints, and success metrics before writing implementation tasks.
Use test-first development and keep review checks visible throughout each phase.
Record architectural decisions and workflow context so later agents can continue with shared state.
anti_patterns: Running npx or local CLI commands without checking the package, version, and working directory.
Skipping specification and architecture work to start implementation immediately.
Launching multiple agents without clear responsibilities, dependencies, and completion criteria.

faq.question: What does SPARC mean?
faq.answer: SPARC means Specification, Pseudocode, Architecture, Refinement, and Completion.

faq.question: Does this skill require Claude Flow?
faq.answer: The methodology can guide any workflow, but the examples use Claude Flow MCP tools and CLI commands.

faq.question: Can Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides structured planning, implementation, testing, review, and documentation guidance for Codex workflows.

faq.question: Is this only for large projects?
faq.answer: No. Small tasks can use a reduced version with clear requirements, tests, review, and completion checks.

faq.question: Does it automatically run commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill documents command examples. Users should approve and verify any CLI command before execution.

faq.question: How should teams start using it?
faq.answer: Start with one feature, define the SPARC phases, assign clear responsibilities, and capture decisions during the workflow.
